$schema-note: Hand-maintained. Data, not code: nothing under src/ imports this file.
purpose: The guard ledger for WIN-258 TRANCHE 5 — `memory`'s canonical store, the
NINTH owner behind the one PostgreSQL client ADR M0.3 §15 gives the ORM. One
entry per guard: per scope predicate, per shape check that stands where a
migration-only CHECK stands, per vocabulary check that keeps a row an older
binary wrote readable, per clause of the one filter translation four reads
share, and per statement the port's contract says must be one statement.
Each carries the file it lives in, the EXACT text that implements it
(`from`), the edit that removes it (`to`), and the NAMED cases that were seen
to go red (`kills`).
IT IS A TENTH FILE beside mutations.json, mutations-identity.json,
mutations-ports.json, mutations-outbox.json, mutations-tools.json,
mutations-agents.json, mutations-cost.json, mutations-channels.json,
mutations-governance.json and mutations-secrets.json rather than an extension
of any of them, for the reason the fourth was: ten tranches are ten separate
claims about ten separate port surfaces, and a reader checking one should not
have to read past the other nine. All are hashed by the same
packages.adapters.config rule and counted together by the v1 ledger.
WHY THIS TRANCHE NEEDED ITS OWN SWEEP. Two of its guards protect columns the
GENERATED CLIENT CANNOT NAME AT ALL. `Memory.embedding` and
`MemoryEntity.embedding` are `Unsupported("vector(1536)")`, so nothing
between a caller's array and pgvector's parser knows how long the column is,
and nothing type-checks the statement that carries it. And FOUR more protect
the `WHERE` of a read: a scope predicate deleted from a `findMany` is a
silent widening that returns MORE rows and fails no type, which is the one
shape a suite written by the same author as the store is least likely to
notice.
procedure: PROVE THE SUITES GREEN FIRST. Tranche 1's first sweep reported 22 kills and
every one was VACUOUS: a context's `dist` had been cleaned, so every suite
failed to load its import and would have 'died' against any mutation at all,
including none. The driver runs each suite set UNMUTATED and refuses to
sweep unless it is green with a non-zero executed case count, and classifies
a run with no executed cases as VACUOUS rather than as a kill.
THE INTEGRATION SUITES RUN ON A REAL POSTGRESQL, in a container, on the
machine that has a daemon. `memory-rows.test.ts` is the only suite here that
runs without one, and it is the one that reaches the mapping branches a
container suite cannot: a container only ever reads rows THIS binary wrote,
so the unknown-vocabulary branches are unreachable from it except through the
one row the constraints suite plants as raw SQL.
EVERY `from` IS A UNIQUE SUBSTRING OF ITS FILE and is applied literally, so a
sweep that silently matched nothing is impossible: the driver refuses an
entry whose `from` occurs zero times or more than once.
RESULT, 2026-09-06, against PostgreSQL 16 (pgvector/pgvector:pg16) in a
container: 40 entries, 40 KILLED, 0 SURVIVED, 0 VACUOUS on the SECOND sweep.
Every baseline suite
set was green with a non-zero executed case count before its mutation was
applied, and every `from` matched its file exactly once.
THE FIRST SWEEP FOUND FIVE SURVIVORS AND ONE UNUSABLE ANCHOR, AND THEY ARE
WHY SIX CASES AND ONE OBSERVATION EXIST.
M-M13 survived because NO READ ON EITHER PORT RETURNS AN EMBEDDING, so a
store that cleared the column on every update looked identical from every
suite; the three cases in `the three-case embedding directive` ask the column
directly instead. M-M16 survived because only one row ever carried the probe
hash, so dropping `sourceThreadId` from a four-column probe changed no
answer. M-M17 survived because the scenario only ever probed a profile as the
agent that WROTE it, for whom the cluster spelling and the agent spelling
resolve the same row — `findProfileRowFromPeer` is the observation that
separates them. M-M18 survived because every id it was given belonged to the
environment it was given. M-M35 survived because NO CALL THROUGH EITHER PORT
CAN EXERCISE IT: the store takes the row id and the environment off the same
aggregate, so a mismatched pair is unreachable — the case that closes it
calls the statement directly rather than arguing an equivalent mutant.
AND M-M34'S ANCHOR MATCHED TWICE. `selectMemoryCandidates` and
`selectEntityCandidates` carry byte-identical agent-scope and
`embedding IS NOT NULL` clauses, so the driver refused the entry rather than
mutating a statement the entry does not name. The anchor now reaches one line
further and is unique. That refusal is the driver doing its job: an entry
that silently mutated the wrong statement would have been scored against the
wrong guard.
